# Overview

Restructured to follow the EXACT analytical pattern of script 5v5
(maternal rank mediation), rather than the earlier generic
predictor-parameterized double loop. Concretely:

  - Script 5v5 runs ONE fixed predictor (maternal_elo_z) through a
    "compile once on draw 1, then update() per subsequent draw" joint
    brms model, looping over a single mediator_specs list, with one
    TEST chunk and one FULL RUN chunk that saves PARTIAL results after
    each mediator and a final combined output at the end.

  - This script now does exactly that TWICE - once for each maternal
    investment predictor (mom_groom_proportion, mom_prox_proportion) -
    as two independent, sequential pipelines, each with its own
    sem_data, its own TEST chunk, and its own FULL RUN chunk. The two
    full runs are then combined at the end into a single results
    table/rds, matching the original script 7 output files.

The underlying model is unchanged from script 7's prior version and
still carries BOTH validated fixes from script 5v5:

  1. weights(obs_weight) implements a FREQUENCY-type weight in brms
     (as if an observation with weight 0.25 contributes a quarter of a
     full observation), not measurement-precision downweighting.
     FIXED: sigma ~ obs_weight (heteroscedastic/distributional
     regression) is used in BOTH equations instead.

  2. Fitting mediator and outcome equations as two SEPARATE brm()
     calls approximates p(a|D1) x p(b|D2), not the genuine joint
     posterior p(a,b|D). FIXED: both equations are fit as ONE joint
     multivariate brms model (bf_mediator + bf_outcome), so a, b, c'
     are drawn together, properly paired, from the same MCMC draws.

Residual correlation (set_rescor) is NOT included - tested in script
5v5 and found not well identified at this sample size.

Convergence must be checked via summarise_draws(as_draws_df(fit)), NOT
posterior::ess_bulk(as_draws_array(fit)) - the latter returned spurious
NA/near-zero values during validation testing.

Predictors (run sequentially, each as its own full script-5-style
pipeline): mom_groom_proportion, mom_prox_proportion.
Mediators (same 6 raw network mediators as script 5v5, reused for both
predictor pipelines): prox_strength, prox_degree, groom_out_strength,
groom_in_strength, groom_out_degree, groom_in_degree. (PC1/PC2 dropped.)
Outcome: elo_one_year_male_male (same-sex-only, matching script
5v4/5v5's convention).

# Compute observation weight (used as a sigma predictor, not a likelihood weight)

```{r compute-weight}
emigrants_full <- emigrants_full %>%
  mutate(
    start_date_effective = if_else(!is.na(DateImmigration1),
                                    DateImmigration1,
                                    DepartureNatalGp),
    window_end = start_date_effective + 365,
    effective_end = if_else(!is.na(LastSeen1) & LastSeen1 < window_end,
                             LastSeen1, window_end),
    days_present_first_year = pmin(as.numeric(effective_end - start_date_effective), 365),
    obs_weight = days_present_first_year / 365
  )
```

# 1. Build maternal investment predictors

## 1a. Maternal grooming investment

```{r maternal-grooming}
emigrants_full$mom_groom_days_to_son <- NA
emigrants_full$mom_total_groom_days <- NA
emigrants_full$mom_groom_proportion <- NA

for (i in seq_len(nrow(emigrants_full))) {
  mom <- emigrants_full$Momcode[i]; son <- emigrants_full$Code[i]
  grp <- emigrants_full$BirthGp[i]; dob <- emigrants_full$DOB[i]
  period_end <- emigrants_full$juvenile_period_end[i]

  if (any(is.na(c(mom, son, grp, dob))) || is.na(period_end) || mom == "" || son == "") next

  mom_groom <- grooming_data %>%
    filter(idindividual1 == mom, group_Abbreviation == grp, date >= dob, date <= period_end)

  if (nrow(mom_groom) == 0) next

  total_days <- n_distinct(mom_groom$date)
  days_to_son <- mom_groom %>% filter(idindividual2 == son) %>% summarise(n = n_distinct(date)) %>% pull(n)

  emigrants_full$mom_groom_days_to_son[i] <- days_to_son
  emigrants_full$mom_total_groom_days[i]  <- total_days
  emigrants_full$mom_groom_proportion[i]  <- days_to_son / total_days
}
```

## 1b. Maternal proximity investment

```{r maternal-proximity}
close_categories <- c("Holding/Clinging", "Contact", "Arm's Length", "Around (<5m)", "<5m")
emigrants_full$mom_prox_with_son <- NA
emigrants_full$mom_son_total_scans <- NA
emigrants_full$mom_prox_proportion <- NA

for (i in seq_len(nrow(emigrants_full))) {
  mom <- emigrants_full$Momcode[i]; son <- emigrants_full$Code[i]
  grp <- emigrants_full$BirthGp[i]; dob <- emigrants_full$DOB[i]
  period_end <- emigrants_full$juvenile_period_end[i]

  if (any(is.na(c(mom, son, grp, dob))) || is.na(period_end) || mom == "" || son == "") next

  mom_scans <- scans %>%
    mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
    filter(tolower(idindividual1) == mom, group_Abbreviation == grp, date >= dob, date <= period_end)

  if (nrow(mom_scans) == 0) next

  n_total <- nrow(mom_scans)
  n_close <- sum(mom_scans$infant %in% close_categories, na.rm = TRUE)

  emigrants_full$mom_prox_with_son[i]   <- n_close
  emigrants_full$mom_son_total_scans[i] <- n_total
  emigrants_full$mom_prox_proportion[i] <- n_close / n_total
}

write.csv(emigrants_full,
          file.path("/Users/alba/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Postdoc_UNIL/Vervet_projects/Pooja_chapter_matrank/Data/emigrants_full_merged.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r filter}
sem_data_groom <- emigrants_full %>%
  filter(!is.na(mom_groom_proportion),
         !is.na(elo_one_year_male_male),
         !is.na(obs_weight))

sem_data_prox <- emigrants_full %>%
  filter(!is.na(mom_prox_proportion),
         !is.na(elo_one_year_male_male),
         !is.na(obs_weight))

cat("Sample size for grooming-investment SEM:", nrow(sem_data_groom), "\n")
cat("Sample size for proximity-investment SEM:", nrow(sem_data_prox), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Diagnostic: compare sem_data_groom vs sem_data_prox
# Run this right after building sem_data_groom / sem_data_prox

# 1. Are they literally the same set of individuals?
codes_groom <- sort(sem_data_groom$Code)
codes_prox  <- sort(sem_data_prox$Code)

cat("Identical Code sets:", identical(codes_groom, codes_prox), "\n")
cat("N groom:", length(codes_groom), " N prox:", length(codes_prox), "\n")
cat("In groom but not prox:", setdiff(codes_groom, codes_prox), "\n")
cat("In prox but not groom:", setdiff(codes_prox, codes_groom), "\n")

# 2. Zero counts in each predictor (proportion == 0 means the mother was
#    observed but never seen grooming/close to the son - different from
#    NA, which means no observation data existed at all for that dyad)
cat("\n--- mom_groom_proportion ---\n")
cat("N non-NA (pre-filter, full emigrants_full):",
    sum(!is.na(emigrants_full$mom_groom_proportion)), "\n")
cat("N exactly 0:", sum(emigrants_full$mom_groom_proportion == 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("N NaN (0/0, i.e. mom had grooming data but zero total groom days):",
    sum(is.nan(emigrants_full$mom_groom_proportion)), "\n")

cat("\n--- mom_prox_proportion ---\n")
cat("N non-NA (pre-filter, full emigrants_full):",
    sum(!is.na(emigrants_full$mom_prox_proportion)), "\n")
cat("N exactly 0:", sum(emigrants_full$mom_prox_proportion == 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("N NaN (0/0, i.e. mom had scan data but zero total scans):",
    sum(is.nan(emigrants_full$mom_prox_proportion)), "\n")

# 3. Zero counts within the actually-filtered sem_data (post sem_data build)
cat("\n--- Within sem_data_groom (n =", nrow(sem_data_groom), ") ---\n")
cat("N exactly 0:", sum(sem_data_groom$mom_groom_proportion == 0), "\n")
print(sem_data_groom$Code[sem_data_groom$mom_groom_proportion == 0])

cat("\n--- Within sem_data_prox (n =", nrow(sem_data_prox), ") ---\n")
cat("N exactly 0:", sum(sem_data_prox$mom_prox_proportion == 0), "\n")
print(sem_data_prox$Code[sem_data_prox$mom_prox_proportion == 0])

# 4. Cross-tab: for individuals in both samples, are the two proportions
#    correlated or suspiciously identical (e.g. accidental copy-paste of
#    one column into the other upstream)?
both <- inner_join(
  sem_data_groom %>% select(Code, mom_groom_proportion),
  sem_data_prox  %>% select(Code, mom_prox_proportion),
  by = "Code"
)
cat("\n--- Cross-check ---\n")
cat("N individuals in both:", nrow(both), "\n")
cat("Correlation (groom vs prox proportion):",
    round(cor(both$mom_groom_proportion, both$mom_prox_proportion, use = "complete.obs"), 3), "\n")
cat("N rows where the two proportions are identical:",
    sum(both$mom_groom_proportion == both$mom_prox_proportion), "\n")
print(head(both, 10))
```

# 3. Mediator specifications (shared across both predictor pipelines)

```{r mediator-specs}
mediator_specs <- list(
  list(name = "prox_strength",      posteriors = prox_posteriors, field = "prox_strength"),
  list(name = "prox_degree",        posteriors = prox_posteriors, field = "prox_degree"),
  list(name = "groom_out_strength", posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_out_strength"),
  list(name = "groom_in_strength",  posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_in_strength"),
  list(name = "groom_out_degree",   posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_out_degree"),
  list(name = "groom_in_degree",    posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_in_degree")
)
```

# 4. Summary helper

```{r summarize-network-draws-function}
summarize_network_draws <- function(estimates) {
  tibble(
    estimate_mean   = mean(estimates),
    estimate_median = median(estimates),
    network_q025    = quantile(estimates, 0.025, names = FALSE),
    network_q975    = quantile(estimates, 0.975, names = FALSE),
    prop_positive   = mean(estimates > 0),
    prop_negative   = mean(estimates < 0)
  )
}
```

# 5. Convergence check helper (uses the VALIDATED reliable method)

```{r convergence-check-function}
check_joint_convergence <- function(fit, rhat_threshold = 1.01, ess_threshold = 400) {
  summ <- summarise_draws(as_draws_df(fit))
  bad_rhat <- summ %>% filter(rhat > rhat_threshold)
  bad_ess  <- summ %>% filter(ess_bulk < ess_threshold | ess_tail < ess_threshold)

  ok <- nrow(bad_rhat) == 0 && nrow(bad_ess) == 0

  if (!ok) {
    cat("    CONVERGENCE WARNING:\n")
    if (nrow(bad_rhat) > 0) {
      cat("    Parameters with Rhat >", rhat_threshold, ":\n")
      print(bad_rhat %>% select(variable, rhat))
    }
    if (nrow(bad_ess) > 0) {
      cat("    Parameters with ESS <", ess_threshold, ":\n")
      print(bad_ess %>% select(variable, ess_bulk, ess_tail))
    }
  }

  list(ok = ok, max_rhat = max(summ$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
       min_ess = min(c(summ$ess_bulk, summ$ess_tail), na.rm = TRUE))
}
```

# 6. Joint Bayesian mediation function (compile once, update() per draw)

Same internal logic as script 5v5's `run_bison_mediation_bayesian_joint`,
generalized only to accept which predictor column/label/sem_data to use
for a given pipeline run - the predictor itself is fixed for the
duration of a full run, exactly as in script 5v5 (it is not looped
inside this function).

```{r joint-bayesian-mediation-function}
run_investment_mediation_bayesian_joint <- function(sem_data, predictor_col, predictor_label, spec,
                                                      num_draws, chains = 2, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000,
                                                      adapt_delta = 0.95) {

  cat("Running JOINT BAYESIAN mediation:", predictor_label, "->", spec$name, "\n")

  males_with_posteriors <- sem_data$Code[sem_data$Code %in% names(spec$posteriors)]
  dat <- sem_data %>% filter(Code %in% males_with_posteriors)

  if (nrow(dat) < 10) {
    cat("  Too few males with posteriors:", nrow(dat), "— skipping\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  cat("  Males with all data:", nrow(dat), "\n")

  first_post <- spec$posteriors[[males_with_posteriors[1]]][[spec$field]]
  actual_draws <- length(first_post)
  num_draws <- min(num_draws, actual_draws)

  mediator_point_estimates <- sapply(dat$Code, function(id) {
    mean(spec$posteriors[[id]][[spec$field]][1:num_draws])
  })
  mediator_center <- mean(mediator_point_estimates)
  mediator_scale   <- sd(mediator_point_estimates)

  build_draw_data <- function(k) {
    dat_k <- dat
    dat_k$mediator <- sapply(dat_k$Code, function(id) spec$posteriors[[id]][[spec$field]][k])
    dat_k$predictor_z <- scale(dat_k[[predictor_col]])[, 1]
    dat_k$male_elo_z  <- scale(dat_k$elo_one_year_male_male)[, 1]
    dat_k$mediator_z  <- (dat_k$mediator - mediator_center) / mediator_scale
    dat_k
  }

  dat_1 <- build_draw_data(1)

  # ── Validated joint model structure: heteroscedastic sigma ~ obs_weight
  # in both equations, NO residual correlation (not well identified at
  # this n - see script 5v5 for validation testing details) ──────────────
  bf_mediator <- bf(mediator_z ~ predictor_z, sigma ~ obs_weight)
  bf_outcome  <- bf(male_elo_z ~ mediator_z + predictor_z, sigma ~ obs_weight)

  cat("  Compiling joint Stan model (draw 1)...\n")
  t0 <- Sys.time()

  fit_base <- brm(
    bf_mediator + bf_outcome + set_rescor(FALSE),
    data = dat_1, family = gaussian(),
    chains = chains, iter = iter, warmup = warmup,
    seed = 1, refresh = 0, silent = 2,
    control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta)
  )

  compile_time <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))
  cat("  Compilation + first fit took", round(compile_time, 1), "seconds\n")

  # Check convergence on draw 1 before proceeding - if this fails, no
  # point continuing to 1,000 more draws with the same problem
  conv1 <- check_joint_convergence(fit_base)
  if (!conv1$ok) {
    cat("  WARNING: draw 1 did not converge cleanly (max Rhat =",
        round(conv1$max_rhat, 4), ", min ESS =", round(conv1$min_ess, 1), ") - inspect before proceeding\n")
  }

  a_all <- numeric(0); b_all <- numeric(0); c_all <- numeric(0); ind_all <- numeric(0)

  for (k in 1:num_draws) {

    dat_k <- if (k == 1) dat_1 else build_draw_data(k)

    fit_k <- if (k == 1) fit_base else update(fit_base, newdata = dat_k, recompile = FALSE, refresh = 0, silent = 2)

    post_k <- as_draws_df(fit_k)

    a_post   <- post_k$b_mediatorz_predictor_z
    b_post   <- post_k$b_maleeloz_mediator_z
    c_post   <- post_k$b_maleeloz_predictor_z
    ind_post <- a_post * b_post   # genuinely paired within-draw, from one joint posterior

    a_all   <- c(a_all, a_post)
    b_all   <- c(b_all, b_post)
    c_all   <- c(c_all, c_post)
    ind_all <- c(ind_all, ind_post)
  }

  results <- bind_rows(
    summarize_network_draws(a_all)   %>% mutate(path = "a (investment -> mediator)"),
    summarize_network_draws(b_all)   %>% mutate(path = "b (mediator -> male elo)"),
    summarize_network_draws(c_all)   %>% mutate(path = "c' (investment -> male elo, direct)"),
    summarize_network_draws(ind_all) %>% mutate(path = "indirect (a * b)")
  ) %>%
    mutate(predictor = predictor_label, mediator = spec$name, n = nrow(dat),
           num_draws = num_draws, .before = 1)

  cat("\n  === Joint Bayesian results:", predictor_label, "->", spec$name,
      "(n =", nrow(dat), ",", num_draws, "network draws) ===\n")
  for (j in 1:nrow(results)) {
    cat(sprintf("  %-35s posterior mean = %6.3f  95%% interval [%6.3f, %6.3f]  %4.1f%% pos\n",
                results$path[j], results$estimate_mean[j],
                results$network_q025[j], results$network_q975[j],
                results$prop_positive[j] * 100))
  }
  cat("\n")

  list(
    summary = results,
    pooled_posterior = tibble(a = a_all, b = b_all, c_prime = c_all, indirect = ind_all),
    draw1_convergence = conv1
  )
}
```

# 7. TEST FIRST: grooming investment, one mediator, small number of draws

```{r test-small-run-groom, eval=FALSE}
test_spec <- mediator_specs[[5]]  # groom_out_degree - matches script 5v5's validated test

t0 <- Sys.time()
test_out_groom <- run_investment_mediation_bayesian_joint(
  sem_data_groom, "mom_groom_proportion", "Maternal grooming investment", test_spec,
  num_draws = 5, chains = 2, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000
)
total_time <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))

cat("\n=== TIMING TEST (grooming) ===\n")
cat("Total time for 5 draws:", round(total_time, 1), "seconds\n")
cat("Draw 1 convergence: max Rhat =", round(test_out_groom$draw1_convergence$max_rhat, 4),
    ", min ESS =", round(test_out_groom$draw1_convergence$min_ess, 1), "\n")

print(as.data.frame(test_out_groom$summary), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 8. FULL RUN — maternal grooming investment (only after confirming timing + convergence above)

```{r run-full-bayesian-groom, eval=T}
all_results_groom <- list()
all_pooled_groom   <- list()

for (spec in mediator_specs) {

  cat("\n>>> Starting grooming ->", spec$name, "at", format(Sys.time()), "\n")

  out <- tryCatch(
    run_investment_mediation_bayesian_joint(
      sem_data_groom, "mom_groom_proportion", "Maternal grooming investment", spec,
      num_draws = 1000, chains = 2, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      cat("  ERROR for grooming ->", spec$name, ":", e$message, "\n")
      NULL
    }
  )

  if (!is.null(out)) {
    all_results_groom[[spec$name]] <- out$summary
    all_pooled_groom[[spec$name]]  <- out$pooled_posterior

    tryCatch({
      saveRDS(all_results_groom,
              "/Users/alba/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Postdoc_UNIL/Vervet_projects/Pooja_chapter_matrank/Data/investment_mediation_bayesian_groom_PARTIAL.rds")
      saveRDS(all_pooled_groom,
              "/Users/alba/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Postdoc_UNIL/Vervet_projects/Pooja_chapter_matrank/Data/investment_pooled_posteriors_bayesian_groom_PARTIAL.rds")
      cat("  Saved progress after grooming ->", spec$name, "\n")
    }, error = function(e) {
      cat("  WARNING: save failed after grooming ->", spec$name, "-", e$message, "\n")
    })
  }
}
```

# 11. Combine both predictor pipelines into the final combined output

Matches script 7's original final output files (single combined CSV/RDS
across both predictors), now built from the two sequential
script-5-style full runs above rather than a single nested loop.

  setNames(all_pooled_prox,  paste("Maternal proximity investment", names(all_pooled_prox),  sep = " -> "))
)
